topic: Zero-Dependency Self-Hosted AI Agent Platform: Personality and Long-Term Memory

key_points: Moltworker lets you run the self-hosted personal agent Moltbot (renamed OpenClaw) on Cloudflare's Sandbox SDK without buying dedicated Mac mini hardware
Containers are ephemeral; sandbox.mountBucket() mounts an R2 bucket as a filesystem so session memory, conversations, and assets persist across container lifecycles
Uses Browser Rendering + a CDP proxy + a browser skill to give the agent browser automation with Puppeteer/Playwright/Stagehand and MCP support
Highlights growing Node.js compatibility in Workers runtime; only ~1.5% of top 1000 npm packages genuinely fail to run
Positions self-hosting as a privacy/cost win versus buying dedicated hardware
Long-term memory is hard: context windows are limited, storing every raw message is expensive, retrieval must be fast and relevant
Solved with a time-stratified design: six temporal grains (working → daily → weekly → monthly → quarterly → yearly), progressive summarization
Pairs summarized logs with a graph knowledge base storing (subject, predicate, object) structured facts for who/what relationships
Keeps recent detail queryable while compressing the past, staying cost-bounded — a concrete architecture for agent memory
mem0 is a 'universal memory layer for AI Agents' with ~63.3K GitHub stars
Adds long-term, persistent memory to agents so they recall users/facts across sessions
Extracts, summarizes, and stores memories; integrates with LLM apps; popular self-hostable option
Microsoft AutoGen (~60.4K stars) is a programming framework for agentic AI
Focuses on multi-agent conversation patterns and orchestration
Shows the mainstream enterprise route to agent platforms (vs self-hosted personal assistants)
LangGraph (~39.7K stars) lets you 'build resilient agents' with explicit graph-based state and control flow
Persistence and state management are first-class — relevant to long-term memory design
Contrast: framework-level building blocks vs turnkey self-hosted platform

stats.fact: The global agentic AI market is valued at USD 7.55 billion in 2025 and projected to reach ~USD 199.05 billion by 2034, a CAGR of 43.2%.
Agentic AI market was valued at USD 5.25 billion in 2024.
OpenClaw (formerly Moltbot/Clawdbot), the self-hosted personal AI agent, has ~386K GitHub stars.
mem0, a self-hostable long-term memory layer for AI agents, has ~63K GitHub stars.
Microsoft AutoGen has ~60K GitHub stars; LangGraph has ~40K — the leading agent frameworks.
In Cloudflare's Workers Node.js compatibility experiment, only ~1.5% of the 1000 most popular npm packages genuinely failed to run.
People were buying Mac minis in bulk to run the open-source self-hosted agent Moltbot on their own hardware.

angles: Zero-dependency framing: run a capable agent fully on your own hardware/cloud with no vendor lock-in — privacy, data sovereignty, and cost control are the core pitch
Personality & long-term memory as the differentiator that separates a useful personal agent from a stateless tool: memory persistence is the hardest engineering problem
Memory architecture deep-dive: time-stratified summarization (working→yearly) + graph knowledge base for structured facts, mirroring how mem0 and LangGraph approach state
Open vs closed/enterprise contrast: OpenClaw (personal, 386K stars) vs AutoGen/LangGraph (framework-level building blocks)
Practical migration path: what you need to run a self-hosted platform today — container persistence (mountBucket pattern), browser automation, local model support (Ollama/llama.cpp)
Cost/effort honesty: self-hosting means you own maintenance, security, and updates; the tradeoff versus cloud-managed agents
